note: Machine-readable claim ledger for the Maneuvers temporal audit. Status vocabulary: STILL SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY SUPPORTED, DISCONFIRMED, UNTESTABLE, OBSOLETE, OVERSTATED, UNDER-SPECIFIED, NOT FOUND, NON-FALSIFIABLE, STILL HYPOTHETICAL (+ combinations). Type vocabulary: OBSERVATION, DEDUCTION, INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS, PREDICTION, SPECULATION (+ combinations).

claims.claim: Routing parasite `0xd4624228`: 2,910 victims; 96.6–98.7% of callers were routers/aggregators; ~100.56 WETH (~$211K) extracted.

claims.confidence: M — direct counts, but reproducibility limited to corpus holders
claims.notes: Micro-cost framing ('each swap pulled a small fee') is an inference layered on the count; per-victim loss ≈ $72 is consistent with a fee skim.
claims.assumptions_required: Router-delivered traffic implies user did not choose the pool.
claims.falsifier: Caller counts not reproducible from stored data.

claims.evidence_at_time: Absence of Transfer logs + unknown selector.
claims.later_evidence: No later evidence in window.
claims.notes: Native ETH value transfers emit no logs by default; a `selfbalance` sweep to an EOA is log-less without any anti-forensic intent. The corpus never states whether the drained asset was ETH or ERC-20, nor considers non-value functions. Alternative hypotheses were not enumerated (V2: 'No alternative hypothesis has been proposed').
claims.assumptions_required: Drained asset is an ERC-20 whose transfer would normally emit.
claims.falsifier: A trace showing the selector moves no value, or moves native ETH only.

claims.claim: Drift recovery: Tether $127.5M + Solana Foundation $20M + $100M revenue credit facility = $247.5M recovered vs $285M loss (~87% coverage); 'every recovery dollar came through external accountability infrastructure'.

claims.source: RPT aethir; V2/V3 A2, A11a; LEX Operational Layer Attack, Participatory Asymmetry
claims.claim: Aethir OFTAdapter (BNB) 2026-04-09, ~$400K gross / <$90K net: owner was a single EOA with no multisig and no timelock; mechanism = private-key compromise 'per the published dev.to post-mortem', which is quoted: 'The legitimate owner was just an eoa…' and 'The protocol had no multisig. They had no time wait mechanism…'.

The dev.to post (cryip, Apr 10) attributes the incident to an unauthorised `transferOwnership` via 'missing or bypassed onlyOwner modifier'; it does not say the owner was an EOA, does not conclude key compromise, and does not contain the quoted sentences. Aethir never published a root cause. DefiLlama: Improper Access Control.
claims.status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (facts) / NOT FOUND (root cause and quotations)
claims.notes: Aethir is the anchor instance for Attack 11a and for 'Operational Layer Attack'. Its classification as key-compromise is unsupported; the only write-up says access-control defect (which would make it Attack 11b-adjacent, not 11a).
claims.assumptions_required: The dev.to post says what the corpus says it says.
claims.falsifier: Aethir root cause statement.

claims.source: RPT kelp; RPT kelp_retrospective; V2/V3 A9; LEX (multiple)

claims.claim: The 1-of-1 DVN configuration was on-chain-readable for ≥56.7 days (blocks 24,500,000–24,900,000) — 'A continuous DVN-configuration monitor … would have flagged this at block 24,500,000 or earlier with zero ambiguity.'
claims.later_evidence: Reproduced. LayerZero's May 18 report adds that the app owner had earlier changed 2-of-2 → 1-of-1 — i.e., the exposure was longer *and* a config-change event existed that a drift monitor would have caught. Dune (Apr 20): 47% of ~2,665 active OApps were 1-of-1, so the flag would have fired on ~1,250 OApps — 'zero ambiguity' about the read, not about prioritisation.
claims.assumptions_required: Prioritisation by TVL is sufficient to make the flag actionable.

claims.status: STILL SUPPORTED (uncertainty was warranted); detection hook C-071 partly invalidated
claims.notes: Correct restraint. The mechanism (poisoned RPC, legitimate keys) is one the corpus's DVN-monitoring hook did not model.

claims.notes: Sui/Move, not an EVM proxy pattern; treat as a key-compromise instance only.

claims.claim: Juicebox V3 (late April 2026): 'access-control / admin-pattern variant', amount pending.
claims.later_evidence: 2026-04-20, ~$52K, REVLoans `borrowFrom()` input-validation / accounting-injection bug in an unprivileged path.
claims.notes: Mislabelled to fit the admin-pattern narrative.

claims.later_evidence: 2026-04-20, Ethereum, ~$50K, first-depositor share-accounting attack; not cross-chain, no admin key.

claims.source: V3 A11b; LEX Distributed Confused Deputy Chain
claims.claim: Renegade 2026-05-10/11, $209K, Arbitrum: unprotected `initialize()` on legacy Dark Pool proxy `0x30bD…DC518`; attacker `0x7772…7777` became admin, delegatecalled malicious logic, drained 27 ERC-20s; 90/10 whitehat return; Blockaid flagged the exposed initializer.
claims.later_evidence: VERIFIED (26–27 tokens; May 10 08:27 UTC; ~$190K returned).

claims.source: V3 validated table; A9/A10/A15; LEX Hybrid Gameboard, Adversarial Maneuver
claims.claim: THORChain 2026-05-15, $7.4–10.8M across BTC/ETH/BNB(/Base): V3 says mechanism 'TBD pending forensics' with four resolution paths; the lexicon (05-17) asserts the mechanism: Bifrost validator signatures cover content but not the inbound/outbound bit of `ObservedTx`; attacker flipped the bit on a real inbound observation and re-proposed; 'THORChain's TSS signs real outbound transactions'; 3,156 ETH 'still held' in a cold wallet.
claims.evidence_at_time: Early press; a separately disclosed V12 Security bug (Apr 28) about unsigned ObservedTx fields.
claims.later_evidence: THORChain Exploit Reports #1 (May 20) and #2 (Jul 3): a GG20 threshold-signature zero-day — a churned-in validator planted a malformed multi-prime Paillier modulus and deliberately failed 864 MtA rounds over 2.5 days to leak other validators' key shares, reconstructed the full vault key and signed outbounds itself, bypassing TSS. THORChain states the V12 ObservedTx bug (patched af46db22, MR 4820) is unrelated. Loss $10.7M; trading resumed June 23; migration to DKLS/FROST. Attacker EVM addresses are now near-empty.
claims.status: V3 hedge STILL SUPPORTED; lexicon mechanism DISCONFIRMED; none of the four enumerated paths matched
claims.notes: The most serious mechanism error in the corpus. A separately disclosed, patched bug was narrated as the exploit two days after the incident and given Go/Chess/Monopoly 'empirical grounding'. The actual class — malicious participant in threshold key generation/signing — was absent from the corpus's enumeration.
claims.falsifier: Official post-mortem (occurred).

claims.claim: THORChain's Mimir parameter-level kill switch (HALTTRADING etc.) stopped the bleed mid-incident — a defensive precedent ('Kill-Switch Governance').
claims.later_evidence: VERIFIED: automatic solvency halts within ~52 min, node pauses, Mimir votes HALTTRADING/HALTSIGNING/HALTCHAINGLOBAL/HALTCHURNING. Q3 2026 saw chain-level halts/rollbacks become the dominant recovery mechanism (Cronos rollback of $111M, Harmony rollback, Cosmos Hub 24.5h halt, Liquid pause, Taiko halt, Osmosis freeze).
claims.status: STILL SUPPORTED; concept elevated by later evidence
claims.notes: One of the corpus's most durable late additions.

claims.source: LEX Hybrid Gameboard, Adversarial Maneuver, Distributed Confused Deputy
claims.claim: Grok/Bankr 2026-05-04, ~$175K: gifted Bankr Club NFT expanded the agent's permissions; prompt injection (masked command) caused an autonomous transfer; attacker's X account deleted within minutes.
claims.later_evidence: VERIFIED (Morse-code reply; Bankr executed Grok's public reply; ~80–88% returned). Followed by Bankr session-key compromise (May 19) and X-account takeover (Jul 25).

claims.source: LEX Protocol-Family Specialist Operator; Configuration-Level Vulnerability
claims.claim: TrustedVolumes / 1inch RFQ proxy 2026-05-06, ~$5.87M; same operator as the March-2025 1inch Fusion V1 incident (per Blockaid); exploited surface = 'signed-quote acceptance scope'.
claims.later_evidence: Amounts and addresses VERIFIED; same-operator claim is Blockaid's and Vladimir Sobolev's without published address linkage; mechanism = permissionless signer registration + validation keyed on the taker + broken replay protection (an access-control/authorization code defect, not a configuration setting). Attacker returned ~1,122 ETH on 2026-07-18.
claims.notes: Classifying an authorization bug as 'configuration-level' stretches the category to cover any misuse of signatures.

claims.claim: Aurellion Labs 2026-05-12 (Arbitrum): attacker called `diamondCut` to attach a malicious facet (`pullERC20`, `sweepERC20`) and swept 456,442 USDC (~99% from one victim) — 'fine-grained per-selector facet registration' sub-mechanism.
claims.later_evidence: Amount/date/diamond/victim concentration VERIFIED. Root cause: an added SafeOwnable facet whose `initialize(address)` was never called — the attacker claimed ownership through the unprotected initializer *first*, then used `diamondCut`. Same class as Renegade (Attack 11b), two days later.
claims.notes: Strengthens 11b (two independent instances in 48 hours) more than it establishes a new 'diamond' sub-mechanism.

claims.source: LEX Forced Deterministic Neutrality, Confused Deputy, Pristine Solo Operator
claims.claim: EXTRACTION_010 (2026-04-30): 'mass dormant-wallet drain' — 5+ (49+) seven-year-old wallets drained by hub `0xA7070344…` in a 3.5-minute burst 'via a valid `transferFrom` signature on a Permit2 approval'.
claims.later_evidence: Event real (hub address matches). Scale: 500–570+ wallets over ~12–13 hours (~261–326 ETH); wallets 4–14 years dormant; **native ETH moved with stolen keys; no Permit2 or approvals involved**.
claims.notes: This event is used as the Permit2 anchor for two core lexicon entries; the anchor is wrong.

claims.source: LEX Cross-Domain Compositional Harm, Confused Deputy
claims.claim: Vercel/Context.ai (disclosed 2026-04-19): Lumma Stealer → Context.ai employee → AWS → OAuth tokens → Vercel employee's 'Allow All' Workspace grant → Vercel internal systems via SSO → env-var enumeration → customer secrets; Vercel CEO attributed attacker velocity to AI — 'first major incident disclosure to name AI-augmented adversary tradecraft'.
claims.later_evidence: Chain VERIFIED except 'SSO into internal systems' (it was Google Workspace account takeover → the employee's Vercel account) and only *non-sensitive* env vars were read. 'First major disclosure' is unverified.

claims.source: V2/V3 A11, A13; LEX Operational Layer Attack
claims.claim: Bybit ($1.5B, 2025) is the canonical large-scale operational-layer attack.
claims.later_evidence: VERIFIED: Safe{Wallet} developer workstation → AWS → malicious JS activated for Bybit's Safe; FBI: TraderTraitor/UNC4899 (same cluster as Kelp).

claims.source: V2/V3 A11; LEX Operational Layer Attack
claims.claim: Blockaid predicted in January 2026 that '2026 attacks will target operational layers around key management, not the keys themselves' — 'empirically validated across Q2'.
claims.later_evidence: No Blockaid January-2026 document with that wording could be located; Blockaid's only January item is an SEC submission without it. Blockaid's *retrospective* April 19 Kelp post and its H1 2026 report (July 28: '74% of stolen crypto value in H1 2026 came from operational and infrastructure compromises') exist.
claims.status: NOT FOUND (citation); substance later SUPPORTED by value-share statistics
claims.notes: Likely a confabulated attribution. The prediction's content is true by value-share, false by incident count (TRM H1: 125/207 incidents were smart-contract exploits).

claims.claim: 'Confirmed by Immunefi community response on April 18, 2026' that compositional/configuration findings are out of scope.
claims.later_evidence: No such Immunefi item located.

claims.source: LEX Bug-Bounty Structural Gap, Proofreading Trap
claims.claim: Cantina rejected a 2026-03-25 submission on `0xd4624228` with the words 'the code did what it was supposed to do'.
claims.notes: Plausible; unverifiable.

claims.claim: 2026-05-11 Ethereum private-key drain by `0xF7CFFC27…` with three victim-mimic vanity wallets (`62ac…EE8A` shape, ~268M attempts each) used for trail confusion and forward poisoning.
claims.later_evidence: On-chain: `0xF7cFFC27…` received 5.8 ETH + a low-cap token from `0x62acE10c…EE8A` on 2026-05-11 and swapped it; the 'victim' was dusted by several look-alike addresses. Total value likely <$20K; the victim sent the funds itself, which fits address poisoning better than key compromise. No public reporting.
claims.status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (mimic cluster exists) / UNDER-SPECIFIED (mechanism, purpose)
claims.notes: A fourth vanity sub-category was created from one tiny incident with an uncertain mechanism.

claims.claim: Central hook: read `EndpointV2.getConfig(configType=2)` on every OApp; alert on `requiredDVNCount < 2` OR `optionalDVNCount + threshold < 2`; correlate with pooled-custody TVL >$10M. Secondary: DVN-operator monitoring ('if a DVN's private key was leaked, signing patterns change').
claims.later_evidence: Central hook adopted industry-wide: Blockaid published an equivalent script on 2026-04-18 (same day as the corpus), Dune dashboard measured 47% 1-of-1 OApps, LayerZero shipped a Config Checker (`less-than-2-dvns`) and raised defaults to 3-of-3 on 2026-07-09; Kelp's own channel now reads 4-of-4. Secondary hook would not have fired for Kelp (keys never leaked; RPC poisoned). The Sandbox exploit (2026-08-21) bypassed threshold monitoring by having the attacker *become* the sole DVN via `approveAndCall` → `setDelegate` → `setConfig` — a config-role capture the hook list omits.
claims.status: STILL SUPPORTED (central hook); PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (secondary); one gap exposed

claims.claim: Initializer-status enumeration: check every proxy for a callable `initialize()`; 'a Tier A on-chain check'.
claims.later_evidence: Aurellion (2026-05-12, two days later) was exactly this class; OWASP SC Top-10 2026 emphasises proxy/upgradeability and SCWE-092 `_disableInitializers` (secondary source). No public tool measured the population of exposed initializers.
claims.notes: Added *after* Renegade; not a prediction, but the fastest-confirmed hook in the corpus.

claims.claim: Pool-lifecycle monitor; oracle-input graph; new-collateral admission monitor; post-admission 90%-drop pressure test.
claims.later_evidence: Moonwell MAMO (Aug 27), Nostra NSTR/Pragma (Sep 17), Tectonic TONIC (Aug 30), Bonzo SAUCE (Jul 11) all match the 'thin-liquidity new collateral → borrow real assets' shape; Lazy Summer (Jul 5) was *stale* valuation of a frozen token; Ostium (Jul 15) was a compromised oracle *signer* with no sanity bounds.
claims.status: STILL SUPPORTED; two sub-modes missing (stale valuation; signer compromise)

claims.claim: Governance-parameter monitor (threshold reduction, timelock removal); durable-nonce lifetime tracking; council-member wallet monitoring; phishing-infrastructure intelligence.
claims.later_evidence: BonkDAO (Jul 6: 1% threshold, no execution delay), Term Finance (Aug 23: thin token vote), Neutron (Sep 22: admin-update proposal executed on passage), AFX (Jul 22: 5-of-7 validator keys). The observed mechanism was mostly *vote capture under no timelock*, not signer phishing; the 'timelock' element of the hook is the load-bearing one.
claims.status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (timelock element confirmed; signer-phishing element not the dominant mode)

claims.claim: Router-percentage spike; multi-perspective probing; empty-log-success detector; balance-delta scanning.
claims.later_evidence: No public instance of routing-parasite or probe-trap classes. JaredFromSubway (2026-06-20, $7.5M) — a top MEV bot drained by 66 approval-trap tokens after ~24h of profitable bait — is the largest public confirmation of the corpus's underlying 'traps target bots' premise, though it used approvals, not router spoofing.
claims.status: STILL HYPOTHETICAL (specific hooks); premise PARTIALLY SUPPORTED

claims.claim: 'Most harm in the permissionless ecosystem is NOT caused by code defects'; code auditing addresses 'a threat model that has stopped being the dominant threat'.
claims.evidence_at_time: April cluster (1 code bug in 3); Drift; Kelp.
claims.later_evidence: By *value*: Blockaid H1 2026 — 74% of stolen value from operational/infrastructure compromise; TRM H1 — infrastructure compromises ~15% of incidents but ~76% of funds. By *count*: smart-contract exploits dominate (TRM: 125/207). Q3 2026: ~$385M (27.9%) from cross-chain *verification code bugs* (Liquid, Gravity, Wanchain, Verus, Secret, Aztec, Syscoin) — code defects, not composition.
claims.status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (value-share) / OVERSTATED (count; code bugs remain a top-two class)
claims.notes: The corpus never defined 'most' as count or value. The Q3 bridge-bug wave is a direct counterexample to 'proofreading has stopped mattering'.
claims.falsifier: Count-share data (occurred).

claims.claim: Capability × permissions × trust bindings × mutability without constraint ('stored potential') is the load-bearing risk indicator; 'The absence of realized value is the danger signal'.
claims.evidence_at_time: Risk-scoring model; Kelp and Drift scored CRITICAL retrospectively.
claims.later_evidence: Descriptively fits Sandbox (attacker EOA dormant 313 days; token-level delegate capability), Humanity (all keys on one laptop), DxSale (2021 locker + owner transfer), Nostra (pre-positioned since March). Counterexamples to 'mutable-admin nodes are the load-bearing risk': Aztec Connect (admin renounced 2023, immutable — exploited via proof bug, $2.1M), Coldcard ($116M — key-generation entropy, outside the node ontology), Liquid ($320M — verification cache bug in an immutable-ish federation).
claims.status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED as a heuristic; discriminative power UNTESTED
claims.notes: No measurement of the discharge rate of CRITICAL-scored nodes versus others exists in the corpus.
claims.falsifier: Discharge-rate comparison across tiers (never done).

claims.claim: A distinct, publicly readable, bounty-out-of-scope failure class exists in deliberate configuration choices; industry-wide DVN exposure.
claims.prediction: Implicit (class will recur; monitoring has lead time).
claims.later_evidence: Strongly supported: Dune 47%/45%/5% (1-of-1/2-of-2/≥3-of-3) on Apr 20; LayerZero Config Checker, 'Production DVN Configuration' docs, 3-of-3 default (Jul 9), DVN refusing sole-attestor role; Brale/Orderly DVN changes; Aave tiering bridged wraps (wrsETH ineligible); Stake DAO (May 27, OFT peer-config redirect, contested) and Sandbox (Aug 21, config-role capture) as post-Kelp instances.
claims.status: STILL SUPPORTED (strongest concept in the corpus)
claims.notes: Formulated 2 days after Kelp; the *specific* hook was independently published by Blockaid the same day, so the corpus's originality is limited, but its generalisation to 'a class' was correct and preceded the ecosystem's policy response.

claims.claim: Lock-and-release custody is the highest-stored-potential cross-chain architecture; mint-burn exploits produce tokens that 'collapse in value', lock-release exploits release real deposits.
claims.later_evidence: Strongly consistent: Sandbox (329T SAND minted, ~$49B face, $675K realised — the realised loss was the Ethereum lock-release adapter drained in <60 s); Symbiosis (46B syBTC minted, $336K realised); Secret (escrow drained by unbacked mints); Gravity ($5.4M custody); Liquid (federation peg-out of ~4,000 BTC = 95% of reserve). Hyperbridge's mint dump realised only ~$2.5M of a 1B-DOT mint.
claims.status: STILL SUPPORTED (with the notional/realised distinction the corpus never made explicit)

claims.claim: When a trusted verifier (oracle, DVN, multisig) fails, downstream components have no mechanism to question the attestation.
claims.later_evidence: Ostium (signed BTC price $5K→$60K accepted on signature alone), Bonzo (Supra oracle contract flaw), Nostra (Pragma mid-pointed a wash-traded pool), Across-Solana (relayer trusted a spoofed event), Wanchain (17-of-25 validators correctly signed an ambiguous message), Bitget (signers accepted destinations from an internal service).
claims.notes: Descriptive, not predictive: it names the seam without saying which verifiers fail.

claims.claim: Code functions correctly; surrounding operational infrastructure (UIs, pipelines, key management, governance workflows) is the compromised layer.
claims.later_evidence: H1/Q3 2026 value-share supports (C-067, C-080); Humanity, Triple-A, Taiko (prover key in GitHub), SingularityNET, Ostium, Bitget ($387.5M: backend request spoofing — signers signed forged requests), LayerZero RPC poisoning. Aethir, the named anchor, is unverified as an ops-layer event (C-043).
claims.status: STILL SUPPORTED (with the weakest anchor removed)
claims.notes: Bitget adds a sub-mode the corpus lacked: signing-pipeline integrity without key theft.

claims.claim: Techniques progress EARLY → ARMS_RACE within ~15 days of public demonstration (Drift→Rhea 15 d; Aethir→Hyperbridge→Kelp 9 d); 'Expect further copies within 30 days'.
claims.later_evidence: Fake-collateral family: no confirmed copy within 30 days of Apr 18 (next public instances: Bonzo Jul 11, Moonwell Aug 27, Nostra Sep 17). Uninitialized-proxy: Renegade→Aurellion 2 days. Governance/no-timelock: Jul 6 → Aug 23 → Sep 22. TSS: THORChain May 15 → Maya Aug 18 (link unverified). Verus repeat 66 days by the same flaw. Lags range 2–95 days; 'ARMS_RACE' also conflates independent replication with same-actor recurrence.
claims.notes: The 15-day figure was fitted to n=2.
claims.assumptions_required: Public demonstration is the propagation trigger.

claims.source: LEX Neutrality Trap (phase 4); Normative Shell Game
claims.claim: Catastrophic losses force centralised overrides (councils, freezes, forks); the surface stays neutral while the periphery accumulates discretionary authority.
claims.evidence_at_time: DAO fork; USDC/USDT freezes; Arbitrum freeze.
claims.later_evidence: Q3 2026: Cronos halted and rolled back 10,961 blocks (reversing $111M); Harmony rollback; Cosmos Hub halted 24.5 h and formed a 4-of-6 recovery multisig; Liquid paused and split; Taiko halted; Osmosis froze allBTC; THORChain Mimir halts; Arbitrum DAO/SDNY litigation over frozen ETH. Chain-level halts/rollbacks became the dominant recovery mechanism.
claims.notes: Directionally right and unusually well borne out; not specific enough to say *which* chains would do it.

claims.claim: Published methodology becomes the calibration target; the sustainable edge is corpus depth.
claims.later_evidence: No evidence either way within the window.

claims.source: LEX Confused Deputy (Agentic AI Supercharger); Distributed Confused Deputy Chain
claims.claim: Agentic AI multiplies confused-deputy incidents; modular protocols with hard-coded mutual trust let one syntactic failure grant protocol-wide authority.
claims.later_evidence: Bankr ×3 (May 4, May 19, Jul 25); Blockaid H2 forecast names prompt injection/tool-use abuse; TRM: AI use in crypto crime +40% YoY; x402 research found violations in all 15 facilitators; dollar losses remain small (~$1M total). Distributed-deputy: Sandbox (`approveAndCall` as the token → endpoint delegate), Humanity (ProxyAdmin → bridge upgrade), Neutron (governance → wasmd admin update → migration).

claims.claim: 'Every successful exploit in the corpus traverses these phases in order… if an exploit cannot be decomposed into these phases, either the taxonomy is incomplete or the exploit is being mis-interpreted.'
claims.testable: No — the escape clause makes it unfalsifiable.
claims.later_evidence: Coldcard (offline brute force of weak seeds: no positioning, no trust establishment, no on-chain reconnaissance); Liquid (proof reuse by parties who then returned 85%); Aztec (three-year-old immutable contract).
claims.notes: Useful as a checklist; false as an empirical law.

claims.claim: Blockchain layers four game mechanics (Go/Poker/Chess/Monopoly); 'the rules are on the board'; every major exploit demonstrates the hybrid nature.
claims.later_evidence: Its THORChain grounding is disconfirmed (C-059); its `0x80b12bd0` grounding is internally contradicted (C-029).
claims.notes: Added 2026-05-17; the last and least disciplined entry.

claims.claim: 'Every attack in Layer 3's corpus is a dynamic behavior failure. None would have been possible on Bitcoin's UTXO model.'
claims.prediction: Implicit (static systems are safe from this class).
claims.later_evidence: Liquid Network (Bitcoin sidechain, Elements range-proof verification cache collision, ~4,000 BTC ≈ $320M); Coldcard ($116M, weak seed generation); Syscoin (UTXO asset commitments). Static-ledger and key-layer failures produced two of the three largest Q3 losses.
claims.status: OVERSTATED / DISCONFIRMED as a general claim

claims.claim: Compute Efficiency Ratio replaces ROI; adversarial systems obey the same thermodynamic constraint; corpus anchors (bb50, 0x3304, f7883, Coffee Fleet).
claims.notes: Philosophy, not a maneuver concept. Aged poorly.

claims.claim: Weber–Fechner JND explains why sub-threshold extraction is invisible; per-victim ~$72 on the router parasite; CE5E's $10K/$20K chunks are above JND by design.
claims.later_evidence: No later evidence.
claims.notes: Applies Weber–Fechner without any behavioural measurement of users.

claims.source: LEX Accountability-as-Load-Bearing; External Accountability Infrastructure; Observational Edge
claims.claim: Layer 3 can observe but not enforce; recovery flows through issuers, foundations, councils, CEX compliance; observational edges collapse if the observer participates.
claims.later_evidence: Recovery in the window came overwhelmingly through external/centralised mechanisms (rollbacks, halts, DeFi United, whitehat deals, CEX freezes). Drift's recovery arithmetic (C-041) was wrong but the direction was right.

claims.claim: Bounties cannot price configuration/operational/compositional findings; the gap is structural.
claims.later_evidence: Ostium's keeper/forwarder path was explicitly out of audit and bounty scope despite an auditor warning; THORChain retired its bounty Mar 31; Cosmos Labs 'wrongly cleared' a valid report then silently patched, exploited ~20h after backport; no Immunefi/Cantina scope-policy change located.

claims.claim: Every claim carries a Tier; Tier C is never used commercially without framing; the corrections index is 'supreme over any other file'.
claims.later_evidence: Violated in the lexicon (retired figures cited live; THORChain mechanism; Aethir quotes; Blockaid/Immunefi citations) and in V3's headline ('the framework's predictions retroactively match the next wave').
claims.notes: The discipline existed and was applied to numbers; it was not applied to narrative and citations.

claims.claim: Top-12-funder exclusion moves the ratio by only +0.9pp (67.1% → 68.1%), so the equilibrium is not an artefact of one operator class.
claims.evidence_at_time: Section A7 of an absent report.
claims.status: UNTESTABLE; note the figures contradict the entry's own 70–79% range

claims.claim: '6-of-14 observed is a material change from v1's 0-of-8. The April wave validated the combinatorial threat-modeling approach: attacks that were hypothetical in v1 either landed as described (Aethir → Attack 2 single-contract) or established new categories that were structurally predictable from the primitives.'
claims.later_evidence: Of V1's eight hypotheticals, none occurred as specified through 2026-09-28. Attack 2 was 'validated' only by relaxing 'fleet of 100+ dormant proxies upgraded in one block' to 'one admin key compromised'. The six 'observed' attacks (5, 9–13) were defined *from* the incidents they are said to have observed. 'Structurally predictable from the primitives' is asserted, not shown (V1 contains no DVN, oracle, or governance primitive).
claims.notes: The central validation narrative of V2 does not survive inspection.
claims.assumptions_required: Post-hoc category creation counts as prediction.

claims.claim: 'v2's combinatorial framework, built two weeks before the May wave, predicted the surface that produced these events… it would have flagged Wasabi (EOA-admin perp adapter), Renegade (unprotected-initializer proxy), and the cross-chain surface generally, before the events occurred. The v3 update reflects observations, not retro-fits.'
claims.later_evidence: V2 (04-20) contains no initializer check; it was added in V3 (05-15) after Renegade. V2's EOA-admin hook was itself derived from Aethir (whose EOA-admin premise is unverified, C-043). 'Cross-chain surface generally' is broad enough to encompass any bridge incident. Volo is Sui; Juicebox/Thetanuts were mislabelled to fit.

claims.claim: Attack 9 generalisation: 'any adapter holding >$10M in pooled deposits with a 1-of-1 DVN is a pre-validated Kelp-class risk' (Tier B).
claims.later_evidence: Population measured by others: 47% of active OApps 1-of-1 (Apr 20). No second exploit of a *pre-existing* 1-of-1 OApp occurred before defaults changed; the one post-Kelp DVN-threshold exploit (Sandbox) created the 1-of-1 condition itself. Massive exposure, low realised discharge — consistent with the class being real and with attackers preferring other seams.
claims.status: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED (exposure real; discharge not repeated)

claims.claim: THORChain resolves to one of: (1) validator-attestation forgery → Attack 9; (2) proof/attestation code defect → Attack 10; (3) validator-key operational compromise → Attack 11a; (4) native-swap settlement asymmetry → new Attack 15.
claims.later_evidence: Actual: a malicious *bonded participant* exploited a cryptographic flaw in the threshold-signature key protocol to extract other validators' key shares. Closest to (2) but at the TSS layer; the corpus had no category for adversarial participation in threshold cryptography.
claims.status: DISCONFIRMED (none of the four); enumeration UNDER-SPECIFIED

claims.claim: 'No v3 additions — the May wave did not produce new instances of this category.'
claims.later_evidence: Correct for May; the category re-appeared from July (Bonzo, Lazy Summer, Moonwell, Tectonic, Nostra).

claims.claim: Of the April–May incidents, vulnerability-centric framing suffices only for Hyperbridge and Renegade; 'the other ten' require the maneuver frame.
claims.later_evidence: Aurellion, Juicebox, Thetanuts, Dango, Silo, TrustedVolumes and THORChain were all code-defect incidents (initializer, input validation, first-depositor, donation logic, oracle misconfig, authorization bug, TSS library flaw). The 2-of-12 count is wrong on the corpus's own evidence once mechanisms are corrected.
